name: Undersea cables & GPS
summary: Finnish court convicts Fitburg crew of aggravated sabotage of Baltic cables; GPS jamming spans NATO's eastern flank
state: On 5 Nov the Helsinki District Court convicted the Fitburg's Russian captain and Azerbaijani boatswain of aggravated sabotage, finding the ship dragged its anchor about 130 km and damaged two cables on 31 Dec; the ruling can be appealed (Yle). GPS interference was mapped along almost the whole eastern NATO flank on 3 Nov (Militarnyi). The verdict concerns a past incident and no new cable cut was reported as of 6 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Most internet traffic reroutes around a damaged cable, so users rarely notice. Airlines and ships near the Baltic and Black Sea may face navigation interference.
rubric_hit: Watch: widespread GNSS interference along NATO's eastern flank; sabotage verdict relates to a December cable incident, no new cut

sources.title: Yle — Helsinki court jails two Fitburg crew members over subsea cable damage
US News — Finland court convicts Russian captain, Azerbaijani crew member over Baltic Sea cable damage
Militarnyi — Large-scale GPS jamming detected along NATO borders

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
